parent.prior: WSP90 DEV_PROSE_RELATION_GROUNDING_FEASIBLE 10/12; trained logistic and handcoded parser both 10/12; curated two choices only

hypothesis: Directly editing raw-character contextual numerical weights from explicit answer-string supervision can extract unseen chemical-symbol and atomic-number answer substrings from entirely new Wikipedia element article prose, rather than choose among externally supplied candidate answers, while retaining old reading skills when demonstrations are appended.
scope: Two fixed question types about chemical elements, both with known answers in training. The model receives the source article and question type plus element name. It emits a source text span or abstains, never receives any answer choice. It scans character boundaries for 1–2 letter (symbol) or 1–3 digit (number) spans; these type priors are predeclared and make this easier than open QA. Training values and groundtruth are in this prereg file but not in the separate text-only source snapshot. Evaluation source family English Wikipedia, same publisher/topic across splits, not independent domain transfer.

source.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 with per-article attribution and contributor history; text only under separate licensed source JSON
source.rules: Fetch exactly specified pages without substitution, preserve requested/resolved titles, page ID, reported latest revision, page URL, history/contributors URL, exact excerpt and SHA256, per-batch response hash; source file excludes every groundtruth symbol/number or role label. Fail closed on missing pages, missing revision, insufficient lead, redirect ambiguity or malformed API response. Freeze snapshot in one source-only GitHub commit before any scoring; code performs no network access during evaluations.
source.license_notice: The TextExtracts API's captured prose cannot be assumed to be reconstructed from the reported revision; stored excerpt bytes/hash are experiment authority. Cite Wikipedia page and contributor history; keep CC BY-SA data separate.

candidate.type: One numeric writer per question relation, 16,384-dimensional hashed overlapping raw Unicode 3-5-char context features surrounding every answer-span candidate. Never use a word tokenizer, transformer, trained LM or gradient updates in candidate.
candidate.span_enumerator: For chemical_symbol enumerate case-sensitive alphabetic substrings of one or two chars bounded by nonletters; for atomic_number enumerate decimal 1–3 digit substrings bounded by nondigits. The enumerator operates on the article's actual characters and yields start/end offsets. No externally provided answer options or QID answer lookup.
candidate.supervision: Initial 8 training articles then 4 additional articles (12 total). Each example provides two correct answer strings, not offsets. Enumerate all exact matching spans and train using averaged positive contexts and balanced negative candidate contexts; reserve all other pages and their answer labels from learner. Direct numerical additive difference-of-class features, no SGD or replay during Stage B.
candidate.output: One extracted source span string, character start/end offsets, and source article/metadata; abstain if no candidate or insufficient score separation. Questions specified as relation ID plus article title; source article provided by evaluator. No arbitrary generative language.
candidate.unknown: Unknown question relation, unknown/unprovided document, nonsensical article with no valid answer should abstain.
candidate.state: Sparse direct numeric weights; deterministic schema-salted SHA256 snapshot with exact numerical restore and corruption rejection. Source attribution separate from weights.
candidate.hypothesis_failure: If source lacks answer span, do not fabricate. Return abstention/error in evaluation report and count as wrong; do not alter frozen articles.

controls.fully_trained_conventional: Independent logistic SGD/span ranker over exactly same raw-character contextual features, positive and negative training spans, 160 deterministic epochs with learning rate 0.75 L2 0.001. Confirm ≥98% training answer exact-match; if not, report underfit and invalidate superiority, rather than comparing to deliberately weak SGD.
controls.symbolic: Explicit regex for Wikipedia patterns 'symbol [A-Za-z]{1,2}' and 'atomic number [0-9]{1,3}', optionally 'chemical symbol'. Independent no-gradient parser, allowed to tie or win.
controls.retrieval: Nearest contextual substring after literal cue 'symbol' / 'atomic number' without supervision, report exact answer.
controls.random: Deterministic candidate span selected from in-article enumerator; report correct.

protocol.stageA: Initial 8 articles ×2 labeled answers =16 supervised fields; score original 8 publicly, freeze snapshot.
protocol.stageB: Four new articles ×2 fields =8 supervised fields. Add direct weights without replay of first 8; fully trained SGD control retrains on all 12 articles and associated labels. Verify cold retention on original 16 learned fields.
protocol.fixture: 8 wholly separate element articles, each two questions; public DEV calibration allowed only here and on 12 trained articles, never reserved titles/answers.
protocol.reserved: 16 different element articles ×2 question types =32 first-use QA questions. All models' outputs frozen and source span hashes computed before scoring against reserved labels. Never rerun these article questions as independent unseen results.

thresholds.caveat: Only a 2-relation chemical-element extractive reader. Cannot claim new knowledge beyond cited source, unseen-domain transfer, language fluency, AGI, GPT/Claude parity or numerical superiority if baselines tie.

qualification: Commit prereg independently before any source/algorithm code.
Fetch 36 predeclared public CC BY-SA Wikipedia articles in at most 2 requests, commit immutable text-only source snapshot and SHA in the isolated repo branch.
Public fixture focused+negative controls without touching any reserved outcomes; candidate tuning only on training and fixture, no edits to reserved source selection/threshold.
Mandatory inherited WSP80..WSP90 tests plus WSP91 focused tests, complete root regression and G29 exact-source atlas on Ubuntu and Windows at the same final SHA.
Only after BOTH OS passes, one original reserved first-use under SHA-pinned CI; publish success or failure with all baselines and resource receipts.
No accepted model/loop merge or promotion without separate authority and scientific independent corroboration.
future: To reach general knowledge, need unseen information across independent documents, questions with no predeclared relation/schema, temporal contradiction, long-term transfer, retrieval over a large corpus and strong fully trained retrieval-neural baselines.
